# Spawn reporting needs a two-sided launch handoff

<a id="body"></a>

## Body

A spawn binding and its caller learning about it are independent facts. Either can happen first: bind then request-drop/timeout must report just as failure then late-bind does. Consuming only at registration loses the former handoff. Match the stored launch's seat AND pane before consumption; a shared spawn_id alone is insufficient, including when Copilot re-registers after /restart. Notify stored Launch.parent, not a replacement registration's parent.

Restart recovery needs durable launched/answered/reported evidence, not merely an unbound-row scan: a bound seat can have lost its answer. Mark reported only after notice admission or an explicit withheld outcome; failed admission remains retryable. In-memory removal is at-most-once consumption, not crash-safe exactly-once model delivery. These complement the existing notification-namespace and Copilot process-incarnation notes.

Regression anchors: spawn_waits tests bind_then_drop_reports_once, another_seat_or_pane_sharing_the_spawn_id_does_not_bind_it, and HTTP a_seat_bound_before_a_restart_cut_its_answer_is_reported_at_boot. Source: #253 at 124ad2f84cfe2d92d477e14731d6003d2a097c23; crates/daemon/src/spawn_waits.rs and registration.rs.

magicWand: one deterministic scenario combining bind, dropped answer and daemon restart.
difficulties: sequential late-bind tests alone miss the reverse transition order.
